subject: chemistry

hotspots.label: Covalent bond
hotspots.description: This band between the atoms is a covalent bond — a shared pair of electrons that both nuclei pull on, gluing the atoms together.
hotspots.positionHint: The soft band between the oxygen and one hydrogen atom.
hotspots.function: Shows the shared-electron bond between two atoms.

hotspots.label: Shared electron pair
hotspots.description: The two small dots between the atoms are the shared pair of electrons — owned by both atoms at once.
hotspots.positionHint: Two small teal dots in the middle of the bond, visible when the shared-pair layer is on.
hotspots.function: Shows the pair of electrons the two atoms share.

hotspots.label: The atoms being joined
hotspots.description: The pale sphere is hydrogen and the red sphere is oxygen — two nonmetals sharing electrons. Neither could steal from the other, so they share.
hotspots.positionHint: The hydrogen (pale) and oxygen (red) spheres of the water molecule.
hotspots.function: Shows the two nonmetal atoms joined by the covalent bond.

visualStyleNotes: Chemistry palette, Anatomy Atelier bar: warm off-white/paper background (#F7F3EC) with a soft radial vignette, no floor grid, no props. The water molecule floats centered, large in frame, lit with soft neutral studio light — no rim-light glow, no bloom, no emissive anywhere. Clean stylized product-render look, specimen-quality not cartoon. Ball-stick style following the app's CPK convention: hydrogen is warm off-white, oxygen is a muted warm red — desaturated a step from the app's data colors so the scene stays calm. Strong saturated color is reserved for the small flat hotspot dots and the shared-pair dots (slate / amber accents from the Chemistry palette). Slow auto-rotation, calm, minimal chrome.
materialNotes: Metallic-roughness PBR, metallic=0 everywhere, single 2K shared texture atlas. Hydrogen spheres: warm off-white matte, roughness ~0.5. Oxygen sphere: muted warm red, roughness ~0.45. Bonds: thin graphite rods between atoms (roughness ~0.55). Shared-pair dots: small teal spheres. No emissive channels anywhere — any glow or pulse is handled by app runtime UI, not baked into the asset.
assetBrief:
SUBJECT: a water molecule built as a ball-stick model, focused on its covalent bonds, built to be read as 'sharing electrons is what holds a molecule together.' Three procedural layers, all clean primitives:

1) MAIN: a ball-stick water molecule — one oxygen sphere (radius ~0.4, muted warm red) at the origin, two hydrogen spheres (radius ~0.26, warm off-white) at ~104.5° positions with bond rods (thin cylinders, graphite, radius ~0.05) connecting each hydrogen to the oxygen. Standard CPK ball-stick.

2) SHARED PAIR (toggleable layer): in the middle of one O–H bond, two small teal electron dots (radius ~0.05) appear side by side — the shared pair. A faint hairline arc links each dot to its nucleus to suggest both atoms pulling.

3) DOUBLE BOND (toggleable layer): the water molecule fades and is replaced by an oxygen molecule (O₂) — two muted-red spheres with TWO parallel bond rods between them (the double bond). Two shared-pair dot pairs sit between the rods.

Camera: framed so the molecule is large and centered with negative space; auto-rotate default. Budget 5-9k triangles. Named nodes: Oxygen, Hydrogen_01, Hydrogen_02, BondRod_01-02, SharedPairDots, O2_Molecule, O2_BondRod_01-02, O2_SharedPairs. All labels are hotspot dots in the app layer.
